sentence: Most of the side effects attributed to the vaccine were mild to moderate — fatigue 59.6%, injection-site pain 59.6%, chills 51.0%.

evidence.span: The most common adverse events attributed to intismeran autogene in combination with KEYTRUDA were fatigue (59.6%), injection site pain (59.6%), and chills (51.0%).
The majority of the adverse events attributed to intismeran autogene were Grade 1 (31.7%) and Grade 2 (51.9%)

why: The release attributes these three rates to the COMBINATION of two drugs. The sentence attributes them to one. It also fuses that with a separate, narrower statement about intismeran autogene alone. Every number is correct and present in the span.
provenance: Live on whatholdsup.org/melanoma from 27 Aug. Found by the operator reading the page on 4 Sep, one hour after the issue was emailed. Survived 8 gate runs, 2 outside reviews and ~90 deterministic checks.

sentence: These are KEYNOTE-942 figures, from the five-year release, which attributes its most common adverse events to the combination rather than to one drug: fatigue 59.6%, injection-site pain 59.6%, chills 51.0%.

evidence.span: The most common adverse events attributed to intismeran autogene in combination with KEYTRUDA were fatigue (59.6%), injection site pain (59.6%), and chills (51.0%).

why: The corrected form. Same numbers, same span, correct subject. A judge that blocks this is producing a false block on the fix for WHU-B-001.
provenance: The 4 September correction.

sentence: Fourteen deaths, seven in each arm — not fourteen patients.

evidence.span: 7 of 107 patients (6.5%) in the intismeran plus pembrolizumab arm and 7 of 50 (14.0%) in the pembrolizumab arm died
157 pts were randomized to intismeran + pembro (n=107) or pembro (n=50)

why: Fourteen patients did die: 7 + 7. The sentence denies a true proposition. The misreading it should deny is that the analysis was OF fourteen people rather than of 157 among whom fourteen died. The source it contradicts is quoted in the same paragraph.
provenance: Live on whatholdsup.org/melanoma. Found by the operator on 4 Sep. Invisible to every figure check because its quantities are spelled as words (GAP-006: 41 such sentences on the page, none bound).

sentence: Fourteen deaths among 157 patients, seven in each arm — not an analysis of fourteen patients.

evidence.span: 7 of 107 patients (6.5%) in the intismeran plus pembrolizumab arm and 7 of 50 (14.0%) in the pembrolizumab arm died
157 pts were randomized to intismeran + pembro (n=107) or pembro (n=50)

why: The corrected form, denying the proposition the label actually invites.
provenance: The 4 September correction.

sentence: Several outlets called it a landmark.

evidence.span: Today’s results represent a landmark moment for adjuvant melanoma treatment

why: The word is the principal investigator's, quoted inside the companies' own release and reproduced by outlets as a quotation. Attributing it to the outlets in their own voice inverts the very distinction the article spends a section drawing.
provenance: Second sentence of the piece. Raised by the fact-check gate on 3 Sep as finding o7 and not actioned until 4 Sep.

sentence: Morning Glory Sciences — an outlet we can find no other publication citing, so we give the argument on its merits rather than on its authority —
why: A universal negative over the whole published literature, resting on one search on one day, used to discount a source the same paragraph then relies on. A 2026 letter in the Irish Journal of Medical Science (DOI 10.1007/s11845-026-04315-0) cites it in reference 12. No span could ever support this sentence.
provenance: Live from 3 Sep. Flagged by the gate as o4 on 3 Sep and not actioned. Found by an outside reviewer on 4 Sep. We could not reproduce the counterexample ourselves: PubMed does not index reference lists and Europe PMC rate-limited every attempt.

sentence: The only survival figure in the programme is descriptive and rests on fourteen deaths.
why: A second survival figure is in a document we hold and had read: the three-year paper reports a hazard ratio of 0.425 on nine deaths. The claim is falsified by our own library.
provenance: Caught by B15 (negatives.py) on its first run, 3 Sep — the one class of proposition error the current deterministic layer does catch.

sentence: The printed figure was out by 0.05 against its own working, for eight days, and nothing here had asked the question until the mark was applied.

evidence.span: the page prints a composite of 3.4; its own working is 3 x .25 + 1 x .20 + 4 x .20 + 4 x .15 + 5 x .10 + 5 x .10 = 3.35

why: 3.35 rounds to 3.4. There was no discrepancy. This is a false accusation against ourselves, published in the correction history — the place a reader goes to decide whether we can be trusted about our own mistakes.
provenance: Introduced BY a correction on 3 Sep. Raised by the gate the same day as o1 and o2, not actioned until 4 Sep.

sentence: Every number above traces to one of these, and none to a news report — a check that runs before this page can publish refuses it otherwise.

evidence.span: the displayed source list showed 9 documents; the bindings named 22; no check compared the two directions

why: No such check existed. B9 runs the opposite way — every LINK must be a source we hold — which a list showing nothing at all would also pass. Thirteen of the twenty-two documents the piece rests on were absent from the list the sentence asks readers to trust.
provenance: Live from 26 Aug. An outside reviewer found one missing source on 4 Sep; checking it properly found thirteen.

sentence: The single most useful question to ask of any interval: does it cross 1.0?

evidence.span: The hazard ratio is an estimate of the ratio of the hazard rate in the treated versus the control group.

why: 1.0 is the no-difference value for a RATIO. For a difference between two rates it is 0. The section explains confidence intervals generally, so 'any interval' is broader than the premise supports. The binding's own step says 'for a ratio'.
provenance: Found by an outside reviewer, 4 Sep, as an Appendix A inference failure.

sentence: The probability of seeing a result at least this good if the treatment actually did nothing. A small p-value means the result would be a surprising fluke.

evidence.span: The P value is then the probability that the chosen test statistic would have been at least as large as its observed value if every model assumption were correct, including the test hypothesis.

why: The definition conditions only on the test hypothesis. The source we cite conditions on EVERY model assumption, and 'fluke' attributes a small p to chance specifically, which is one of the misinterpretations that paper exists to list. The page's own next callout already said so — it contradicted itself across two adjacent boxes.
provenance: Found by an outside reviewer, 4 Sep. The source is one we hold, cite and had read.

sentence: A CTLA-4 inhibitor is a different drug against a different target, and this page holds no document about one.

evidence.span: "label":"Ipilimumab and Placebo matching Nivolumab"

why: The preceding sentence says CheckMate 238's arms are nivolumab and ipilimumab, and we hold its registry record. Ipilimumab is a CTLA-4 antibody. The page holds a document about one, and says so two sentences earlier.
provenance: Found by an outside reviewer, 4 Sep. Listed in our own review packet as a claim 'checkable against Appendix B' — it was checked and it failed.

sentence: It is a figure from 157 patients in an open-label study, not the result announced this month — and it describes a rate of recurrence, not a share of patients cured.

evidence.span: reducing the risk of recurrence or death by 49%

why: The endpoint is recurrence-OR-DEATH. Dropping 'or death' understates what the composite counts. This is rule 3 of the publication's own editorial standard, and it has produced findings in three consecutive reviews.
provenance: Found by an outside reviewer, 4 Sep. Three other instances had been corrected the day before.

sentence: 0 Phase 3 efficacy numbers released

evidence.span: The trial met its primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS) and a key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS).
"hasResults":false

why: The premises support a zero over the documents this issue holds. The card asserts a zero over the world. The binding's own recorded step said so in capitals — 'THE CARD DOES NOT SAY THAT' — and the card shipped anyway.
provenance: A defect we had recorded ourselves and published regardless. Found by an outside reviewer, 4 Sep, who was handed our own note admitting it.

sentence: Those newly-included patients start at lower risk of recurrence, which leaves less room for absolute benefit, and Pharmacy Times’ counter is that their risk may be closer to stage III than the staging suggests.

evidence.span: The Phase 2b population was stage IIIB-IV; the Phase 3 adds stage IIB and IIC - node-negative disease .
patients with resected stage IIB or IIC melanoma can face risks of recurrence and melanoma-specific mortality similar to those observed in stage III disease

why: The paragraph above says 'Which of them is right cannot be settled from anything published.' This sentence then settles it for one side and demotes the other to a 'counter'. Both spans are accurate; the framing is not.
provenance: Found by an outside reviewer, 4 Sep. Verifiable entirely inside the piece, with no external source needed.

sentence: [CORRECTION] We removed '29 blocks of four' because no reachable source states a block count.

evidence.span: Legible patients were randomised into either arm using 29 blocks with block size of four.

why: The correction deleted a TRUE statement. The paper says it, in its Methods. The withdrawal was written from a fact-check finding by someone who had not opened the paper. Every control in the system asks whether a claim is supported; none asks whether a DELETION was.
provenance: CORR-13 on issue two. Reverted 1 Sep. The single strongest case for treating corrections as first-class releases.

sentence: MONALEESA-7 [cited with PALOMA-2's registry number]

evidence.span: the two trials carry different NCT identifiers

why: A registry identifier attached to the wrong trial. Mechanically settleable from a structured field, and it came in with an earlier correction.
provenance: CORR-06 on issue two, introduced by CORR-02.

sentence: HARMONIA found no difference between the two drugs.

evidence.span: HARMONIA has not reported results

why: A trial credited with a finding it never reported. Settleable from a registry field, free and exact. Three separate sentences on that page made this error and all three came in with an earlier correction.
provenance: CORR-12, CORR-15 and CORR-17 on issue two, all introduced by CORR-01.

sentence: By the three-year readout the recurrence interval cleared the no-effect line.

evidence.span: These subsequent analyses are not intended for formal hypothesis testing (ie, are descriptive only).

why: 'Cleared' implies a threshold was crossed in a test. The paper says its analyses are descriptive only. The interval stopped including 1.0; nobody crossed anything.
provenance: Caught 2 Sep by an adversarial check. The distinction it turns on — confidence in direction versus a formal test — is rule 8 of the editorial standard.

sentence: In the earlier Phase 2b at five years, patients on the combination were recurring or dying at about half the rate (HR 0.51, 0.294–0.887).

evidence.span: reducing the risk of recurrence or death by 49% (HR=0.51; [95% CI, 0.294-0.887])

why: Composite preserved ('recurring or dying'), figures exact and at the precision the source prints, subject correct, scope correct. A judge that blocks this is over-triggering.
provenance: Published and never corrected. Written as HR 0.510 in the first draft of this case file — the release prints 0.51, and the benchmark's own span test caught the extra digit before the file was committed.

sentence: For adjuvant PD-1 inhibitors specifically — the comparison arm in this very trial — neither of the two placebo-controlled trials whose registry records we hold — KEYNOTE-054 and KEYNOTE-716 — has posted an overall-survival result at all. That is an absence of a finding, not a null one.

evidence.span: "reportingStatus":"NOT_POSTED","anticipatedPostingDate":"2026-11"
"reportingStatus":"NOT_POSTED","anticipatedPostingDate":"2033-10"

why: A universal negative that is correctly SCOPED to two named registry records we hold, and that names the distinction between an absent finding and a null one. This is the shape a defensible negative takes; a judge must not block it merely for containing 'neither'.
provenance: Rewritten 3 Sep after an earlier version overreached, and survived the 4 September outside review.

sentence: CheckMate 238’s arms are nivolumab and ipilimumab, so there is no placebo arm to report against.

evidence.span: "label":"Ipilimumab and Placebo matching Nivolumab"

why: The word 'Placebo' appears in the span and the sentence correctly says there is no placebo ARM — the placebos are the matching dummies that keep the trial blinded. A judge that reads 'Placebo' in the span and clears a claim that the trial has placebo data is making the error a counterexample hunt actually made here at high confidence.
provenance: Rewritten 3 Sep precisely because an adversarial run misread these labels.

sentence: The release reports a hazard ratio of 0.510 for recurrence or death.

evidence.span: reducing the risk of recurrence or death by 49% (HR=0.51; [95% CI, 0.294-0.887])

why: The release prints 0.51. Writing 0.510 shows a significant figure the source does not, which asserts a precision nobody measured. The peer-reviewed paper does print 0.510, so the figure is not wrong — the attribution of that precision to THIS document is.
provenance: Found while building this benchmark: the span test rejected a case file entry written from memory as 0.510. The live page carries 0.510 credited to the release. B12 flags this class and it is a real instance.
